doe-osti-2589836-parallel-programming-in:
Jerawan Armstrong explains the parallel running modes of MCNP6 in Los Alamos National Laboratory report LA-UR-25-29475, issued 22 September 2025. MCNP is the laboratory's general Monte Carlo code for tracking particles through matter, used in shielding, reactor, and safety work. Long runs need many processors at once, and the code offers two ways to share the work.

OpenMP threads split a job across cores inside one machine, sharing memory. MPI splits it across many machines that pass messages. Users can run either mode alone or a hybrid of both, matched to the computer and the problem. The short guide walks through how each mode behaves and where each fits, from a desktop to a computing cluster. New users get a plain map of choices that strongly affect run time.
